bio: I've spent more than seven years on Angular front ends and the .NET APIs behind them, across healthcare, UN and enterprise products, at [four companies](#experience) in Nagpur and Pune.

Most of that work now is micro frontends: splitting monoliths into apps that can ship on their own, building the shared UI libraries that keep them consistent, and putting YARP gateways in front of the services.
Outside the day job I build [Samyo](https://samyo.in), maintain a couple of [Angular libraries on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/~devendramilmile), and [write up what I learn](/blogs).

projects.title: Samyo
projects.description: My own SaaS for small event businesses in India: balloon decorators, DJs, photographers, stage and lighting crews. It replaces the paper booking diary with one app for bookings, equipment, payments, and team assignments.
highlights: Reminders on WhatsApp, email, or push 7 days, 2 days, and 4 hours before each event
Equipment checklists generated from the services each business offers
Works offline at the venue and installs on a phone
Interface in English, Hindi, and Marathi
projects.summary: Booking and operations app for event businesses

image.alt: Samyo's landing page: "Stop forgetting bookings", beside the app's dashboard on a phone

projects.title: @datelane/core
projects.description: An Angular scheduler and calendar library with no runtime dependencies. Date handling is pluggable, so it works with native Dates, Luxon, or Moment. MIT licensed and on npm.
highlights: 12 views: day, week, month, year, agenda and timeline
Drag to move and resize, recurring events, resources
Dark mode and right-to-left layouts
Pluggable date adapters: Native, Luxon, Moment
Zero runtime dependencies

image.alt: datelane week view: colored events across seven days, an all-day band, and a red line marking the current time

video.label: datelane demo: an event is dragged from Tuesday to Thursday, another is resized by its bottom edge, then the view switches through Month and Timeline Week back to Week
